summary: Module 05 reconciled with the real lab outputs of commit 8bf3ba8 and given its module-level edit. node tools/check.mjs --module 5 --lang en --words reports 0 errors and 0 warnings (fig-05-13 is already drawn, so not even that warning remains); concept prose is 16,626 words against a target of 15,650 (s1 1044, s2 1079, s3 1675, s4 1163, s5 1924, s6 1394, s7 1538, s8 1288, s9 1894, s10 896, s11 1037, s12 961, s13 733). Every sentence, table, caption, exercise, quiz explanation and summary line that quotes a lab now matches the printed outputs; where a qualitative claim failed it was rewritten to what was measured: Lab 3's plain GCN peaks at 8 layers (0.959) and only 12 and 16 layers collapse to the majority class (0.781, not 0.838); Lab 4's non-dimensional PINN reaches 0.0004 at 7,500 steps but reads 0.0073 at 10,000 because the error oscillates at a fixed learning rate; Lab 5's no-shift confusion errors are now mostly misalignment-as-imbalance (18) rather than bearing-as-healthy (13); and Lab 2's 0.999 cap did not make w = 7 diverge in a retrained copy. Claims that needed evidence beyond the printed runs were checked with copies of the lab code in the scratch folder (bash tools/labpy.sh): Lab 1 KL warm-up (beta ramp to 1: 8 active units, KL 3.48; ramp to 4: KL 0.01, 0 active), Lab 2 with QUICK = True (precision-like 0.039, recall-like 0.025), with the 0.999 cap (w = 7 precision-like 0.019, recall-like 0.043) and with the linear schedule (0.020, 0.022; alpha-bar_T 0.132), Lab 4 curve_d every 100 steps (0.0001-0.016 after step 6,000, minimum 0.00006 at 8,700; weighted run 0.004-0.013 over its last 1,000 steps) and the hard-constraint extension (0.090 at 10,000 steps), Lab 5 with gain range 0.25-4 (0.956/0.990/0.997), Exercise 12's solution code (re-run twice, reproducible; outputs differed from the fence, which was replaced), and the hand-computed numbers of s5, s6, s8 and s9 with NumPy/SciPy (all confirmed except solve_ivp's 7e-9, which needs atol 1e-10, now stated). Lab 1 and Lab 3 code changed slightly (a checker false positive and a wrong plot title); both were re-run with --update and then without it: Lab 3 reproduces exactly, Lab 1 apart from its wall-clock seconds. The plan JSON is valid; its display fields, activity refs, lab runtimes, s1's worked example and one paper question were changed.

Proposed fix: one plan-sync pass that copies the numbers from the reconciled text, or a note in the plan that its lab numbers are planning values superseded by the text, so a translator or later writer does not reintroduce them.

Lab 4's non-dimensional run and its weighted run both oscillate at a fixed Adam learning rate, so the step-10,000 snapshot (0.0073) is worse than the weighted run's (0.0039) and the 'ten times better' story holds only at the 7,500-step snapshot. The text now says so. A cleaner lab would add a cosine learning-rate decay (or report the best error on the recorded curve) to Steps 5-6; that changes lab code and every Lab 4 number quoted in s9, What goes wrong and the quiz, so it was not done here. Proposed fix: decide in the next lab pass whether to add the decay and re-reconcile.

Lab 2's cap at 0.5 is now presented as a safeguard rather than a necessity, because a retrained copy with the paper's 0.999 clip gave good guided samples in this environment (precision-like 0.019 at w = 7); the divergence (1.34) survives only as a prototype result. If a lab that demonstrates the failure is wanted, Try-this item 1 could ask the reader to raise w beyond 7 or shorten training; untested.

Exercise 12's output fence and Section 9's derived numbers come from runs in the scratch folder, not from tools/labrun.py, which only executes lab sections. They reproduce exactly on this machine (one thread), but the build will not detect drift. Proposed fix: none needed now; re-run e12 whenever the PyTorch version changes.
Lab 1 reproduces exactly except its wall-clock seconds (11/10 s against 12/10 s); this is the expected timing noise.
